top_opportunities.title: [Bounty proposal] fix(goals): get_user_goals drops active goals by limiting before filtering ($50)
top_opportunities.description:
Fixes #22778. PR: #23293**Bug:** `get_user_goals` (backend/database/goals.py) applied `.limit(limit)` inside the Firestore query, so the page filled in document-id order BEFORE the achieved/abandoned filter ran. If a user's first page is all ended goals, active goals get dropped and callers asking for `limit` active goals silently receive fewer. Callers affected: `backend/utils/proactivity_producers.py` and `backend/utils/llm/external_integrations.py` (both pass limit=3).

**Fix:** the bound now applies after the ended-goal filter and the oldest-first `created_at` sort — the same pattern `get_all_goals` in the same module already uses and documents for exactly this reason. 6 lines, no schema/API changes.

**Bounty**: $50 USD on merge, paid via Algora. — NoYouDeal

`tokens/token-swap` ships only the `anchor/` flavor. Sibling token examples (`create-token`, `transfer-tokens`, `escrow`, `pda-mint-authority`, `nft-operations`) teach the same operations across anchor/native/pinocchio so learners can diff what each framework generates and costs.

## Precedent

The Solana Foundation's recent program-examples bounty rounds paid $200-500 per framework per program for exactly this kind of flavor coverage (Token Swap was one of the funded examples in Steel/Poseidon). Extending the in-repo anchor flavor to `native/` is the same educational value, in-repo.

- `tokens/token-swap/native/`: `program/` crate added as a root workspace member (or listed in `.github/.workspace-ignore` per CI rules), `package.json` with mandatory `build-and-test` script, tests on the repo's test stack — mocha + tsx, `@solana/kit` + `litesvm` 1.x, `FailedTransactionMetadata` assertions, `svm.expireBlockhash()` between identical resends.

top_opportunities.title: [puzzle] Deadlock detection for boxes stuck in corners
top_opportunities.description:
**App:** `apps/puzzle`
**Amount:** not yet funded
**Base commit:** `5c76d40`
**Checker:** [`bounties/puzzle-deadlock/check.yml`](https://github.com/amiller/bounty-arcade/blob/8232383/bounties/puzzle-deadlock/check.yml) at `8232383`, run with `node check.mjs bounties/puzzle-deadlock/check.yml ` in the dev image. Nobody reviews the result.

A box pushed into a corner that is not a goal can never move again, and the
player only finds out much later. Add `deadBoxes(state)` to `logic.js`, returning
the sorted indices of boxes that sit on a non-goal cell with a wall on one
vertical side and one horizontal side. The UI marks those cells with a `dead`
class and shows "Stuck: a box is in a corner" in `#status`.

Acceptance tests (`test/deadlock.test.js`):
- `deadBoxes returns [] for every level's start`: `deadBoxes(parse(lv.map))` deep-equals `[]` for each entry in `levels.json`.
- `corner box is dead`: `deadBoxes(play(parse(levels[1].map), 'DLdR'))` (level "Corner") deep-equals `[28]`.
- `dead box in a larger level`: `deadBoxes(play(parse(levels[4].map), 'URurDD'))` (level "Storeroom") deep-equals `[33]`.
- `box on a goal in a corner is not dead`: `deadBoxes(parse(['####', '#@*#', '####']))` deep-equals `[]`.
- `wall on one side only is not dead`: `deadBoxes(parse(['######', '#@$ .#', '#    #', '######']))` deep-equals `[]`.
- Playwright `marks dead box`: select option value `1` ("Corner"), press `ArrowDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowRight`; assert `#board .dead` has count 1, it is the 29th `.cell` (index 28), and `#status` contains `Stuck`. Then click `undo` and assert `#board .dead` has count 0.

top_opportunities.title: [puzzle] Persist progress and best scores per level
top_opportunities.description:
**App:** `apps/puzzle`

**Checker:** [`bounties/puzzle-progress/check.yml`](https://github.com/amiller/bounty-arcade/blob/8232383/bounties/puzzle-progress/check.yml) at `8232383`, run with `node check.mjs bounties/puzzle-progress/check.yml ` in the dev image. Nobody reviews the result.

Players lose their place on reload. Store, per level name, whether it was solved
and the fewest moves used, and restore the last selected level on load. Keep the
bookkeeping pure in `logic.js` as `recordWin(progress, levelName, moves)` returning
a new progress object; `ui.js` reads and writes it under the `localStorage` key
`puzzle-progress`. The level `` shows a check mark and the best move count
for solved levels.

Acceptance tests (`test/progress.test.js` and `test/progress.spec.js`):
- `recordWin stores first result`: `recordWin({}, 'Corner', 12)` deep-equals `{ Corner: { best: 12 } }`.
- `recordWin keeps the lower count`: `recordWin({ Corner: { best: 12 } }, 'Corner', 20).Corner.best === 12` and with `9` it is `9`.
- `recordWin does not mutate input`: the argument object is unchanged after the call.
- Playwright `best score survives reload`: solve level 1 with `ArrowRight` x3, reload, assert the option with value `0` contains `3` and a check mark (`✓`).
- Playwright `last level is restored`: select option value `2`, reload, assert `#level` has value `2` and `#moves` is `0`.

top_opportunities.title: [puzzle] Shareable replay links
top_opportunities.description:
**App:** `apps/puzzle`
**Amount:** not yet funded
**Base commit:** `5c76d40`
**Checker:** [`bounties/puzzle-replay-links/check.yml`](https://github.com/amiller/bounty-arcade/blob/8232383/bounties/puzzle-replay-links/check.yml) at `8232383`, run with `node check.mjs bounties/puzzle-replay-links/check.yml ` in the dev image. Nobody reviews the result.

Let a player share a solution as a URL such as `/apps/puzzle/#level=2&moves=lLLLrrrddLLL`.
On load, the page selects that level and replays the moves; the replay must stop
with an error message in `#status` if a move is blocked. Add `replayUrl(levelIndex, state)`
and `parseReplay(hash)` to `logic.js`, and a "Copy link" button with
`data-testid="share"` that writes the URL to `#share-url` (a read-only input).

Acceptance tests (`test/replay.test.js` and `test/replay.spec.js`):
- `parseReplay round-trips`: `parseReplay('#level=2&moves=lLLLrrrddLLL')` deep-equals `{ level: 2, moves: 'lLLLrrrddLLL' }`.
- `replayUrl encodes history`: `replayUrl(0, play(parse(levels[0].map), 'rRR'))` equals `'#level=0&moves=rRR'`.
- `parseReplay rejects junk`: `parseReplay('#level=x&moves=q')` throws.
- Playwright `replay link solves a level`: goto `/apps/puzzle/#level=2&moves=lLLLrrrddLLL`, assert `#level` value `2`, `#moves` text `12`, `#status` contains `Solved`.
- Playwright `blocked replay reports the step`: goto `/apps/puzzle/#level=0&moves=l`, assert `#status` contains `blocked` and `#moves` is `0`.

top_opportunities.title: [routes] Segments and gaps
top_opportunities.description:
**App:** `apps/routes`
**Amount:** not yet funded
**Base commit:** `5c76d40`
**Checker:** [`bounties/routes-segments/check.yml`](https://github.com/amiller/bounty-arcade/blob/8232383/bounties/routes-segments/check.yml) at `8232383`, run with `node check.mjs bounties/routes-segments/check.yml ` in the dev image. Nobody reviews the result.

`parseGpx` flattens every `` into one list, so a GPX with two `` blocks (a paused recording, or a ferry crossing) counts the straight line across the gap as distance. Return `segments: [[point, ...], ...]` alongside `points` (`points` stays the flat list), and add `stats(points, { segments })` (default `[points]`) whose distance and gain/loss sum within segments only. Draw each segment as its own `` in `#track`.

Acceptance tests (`bounties/routes-segments/`):
- `parses two segments`: a GPX string with two `` blocks of 2 and 3 points gives `segments.length === 2`, lengths `[2, 3]`, and `points.length === 5`.
- `distance skips gaps`: segments `[(0,0),(0,0.01)]` and `[(10,10),(10,10.01)]` give `stats(points, { segments }).distance` within 1 m of `haversine((0,0),(0,0.01)) + haversine((10,10),(10,10.01))`.
- `gain skips gaps`: segment elevations `[100, 110]` and `[500, 490]` give gain 10 and loss 10.
- `samples unchanged`: both bundled samples have one segment and `stats(points, { segments })` gives the same distance as before (4020.8 m and 9105.4 m, within 1 m).
- Browser: uploading a file with segments (0,0)–(0,0.01) and (0.01,0.01)–(0.01,0.02)–(0.02,0.02) via `#file` yields `#track polyline` count 2 and `#stat-distance` `3.34 km` (4.45 km with the gap).
